ITE.title: External Thermal Insulation (ITE)
ITE.leadDesc: Financial aid helps you carry out your exterior thermal insulation work at a lower cost. Enjoy optimal comfort all year round: a warm interior in winter and cool in summer, while saving up to 9,000 euros through subsidies.
ITE.leadLink: Learn more on the official ministry website by clicking here.
ITE.asterisk: * Subject to eligibility. Amount varies according to income conditions.
ITE.eduP1: External Thermal Insulation (ITE) improves the energy efficiency of your building by reducing heat loss through exterior walls.
ITE.eduP2: The process involves adding a layer of insulation to the outside walls, then covering it with a protective finishing coat. This creates a true thermal barrier between the inside and outside.
ITE.eduP3: By eliminating thermal bridges, ITE significantly reduces your heating and cooling needs, protects your building's structure against bad weather, and durably improves your comfort while rejuvenating your facade's aesthetics.
ITE.step1d: Removal of existing coating, temporary removal of fixings and protruding elements if necessary, cleaning and preparation of the surface for insulation.
ITE.step2d: Installation of thermal insulation. Suitable materials are fixed using special adhesives or mechanical anchors, avoiding any thermal bridges.
ITE.step3d: Treatment of joints to ensure thermal continuity and prevent air infiltration. Use of fixings to seal everything.
ITE.step4d: Application of the coating which protects the insulation and offers an aesthetic finish. The coating is selected according to your preferences and building constraints.
ITE.step5d: Reinstallation of architectural elements removed during preparation. Complete cleaning of the work area and removal of rubble.

PAC.title: Heat Pump (PAC)
PAC.leadDesc: Replace your old heating system with a modern, high-performance heat pump. You enjoy gentle heat in winter while considerably reducing your carbon footprint and energy bills, with government aid to finance your project.
PAC.asterisk: * Maximum estimated amount subject to eligibility for various ecological transition premiums.
PAC.eduP1: A heat pump is a heating system that uses heat transfer. It extracts calories naturally present in the air or water outside to transfer them inside your building.
PAC.eduP2: Thanks to a thermodynamic cycle (with a refrigerant, an evaporator, a compressor, and a condenser), the PAC produces more energy than it consumes. Some reversible models can even cool your interior in summer.
PAC.eduP3: It's an ecological and highly efficient solution that reduces the use of fossil fuels, lowers greenhouse gas emissions, and lightens your bills while improving your comfort.
PAC.typesDesc: The main difference lies in the heat source and the delivery method. The choice depends on your climate, space, and preferences.
PAC.type1d: It uses ambient air as a heat source. The system extracts calories from the outside air and diffuses them directly as hot air inside your home via wall units (splits). Ideal for fast heating and often reversible (air conditioning).
PAC.type2d: It also extracts heat from the outside air but transfers it to the water in your central heating circuit (radiators, underfloor heating). It can also produce your Domestic Hot Water (DHW). It's the ideal solution to replace an oil or gas boiler.
PAC.step1d: Determining the optimal location considering sun exposure and access.
PAC.step2d: Preparing the site with a stable, leveled surface. Optimizing efficiency.
PAC.step3d: Mounting the PAC safely on its base. Use of anti-vibration mounts.
PAC.step4d: Installing and sealing pipes and cables. Setting up the waterproofing.
PAC.step5d: Commissioning tests, final adjustments, and training the client on usage.

TH145.title: BAR-TH-145 Program
TH145.desc: High-performance global renovation for an energy-efficient building.
TH145.leadDesc: The BAR-TH-145 program offers generous aid for global thermal renovation projects. The principle presented: there is only a minimal out-of-pocket expense for the owner, sometimes as low as 1 euro, subject to eligibility. This system aims to encourage global renovations to improve energy efficiency while reducing the financial burden.
TH145.leadLink: Learn more on the official ministry website by clicking here.
TH145.asterisk: * Subject to eligibility. Out-of-pocket expenses depend on the situation and program criteria.
TH145.eduP: The BAR-TH-145 sheet is a complete global building renovation solution, set up by public authorities within the framework of Energy Savings Certificates (CEE). It allows owners to receive significant financial support for a bundle of works (insulation, heating system replacement, ventilation) aimed at significantly reducing energy consumption.
TH145.inst1d: Insulation improves the home's energy efficiency by reducing heat loss, lowering heating costs, and significantly increasing comfort.
TH145.inst2d: Replacing an existing heating system with a modern, energy-efficient solution improves comfort while reducing energy use and CO2 emissions.
TH145.inst3d: The thermodynamic water heater provides domestic hot water in an energy-efficient manner, thereby reducing energy consumption and associated costs.
